alternatives: FastAPI directly managing remote device processes
consequences: Restart Agent progress must reflect actual delivery and recovery
Supervisor absence produces guidance rather than fake repair
entities.context: The canonical architecture separates command execution, reconnect recovery, and stopped-agent recovery.
entities.description: Joined-device execution stays in the node agent and recovery stays in a separate supervisor/watchdog path.
entities.name: Agents and supervisors own device execution and recovery
runtime_implications: Running-but-disconnected and stopped-agent recovery remain distinct
security_implications: Protected agent identity stays on the managed device
trade_offs: Keeps remote execution local to the managed device

entities.context: Device onboarding must fail closed on identity mismatch and prevent duplicate or protected-host enrollment conflicts.
entities.description: Device invites and bootstrap commands are generated by backend services after duplicate and identity checks.
entities.name: Bootstrap artifacts are backend-generated and identity-guarded
runtime_implications: Identity mismatches fail before environment or PM2 mutation
security_implications: Invite/bootstrap secrets are not exported into documentation
trade_offs: Prevents browser-held enrollment secrets and unsafe identity overwrite

consequences: Prepared projections may be stale while durable state remains authoritative
Operational health and semantic parity remain independent
entities.context: The architecture model distinguishes durable-state components from projections and requires truthful reconciliation.
entities.description: Durable control-plane records remain in SQLite while prepared projections optimize bounded reads.
entities.name: SQLite is durable authority for control-plane state
runtime_implications: Projection freshness can gate writes without deleting durable history
trade_offs: Preserves durable recovery and auditable state

alternatives: Generate tracked docs directly from the current phone
consequences: Observed does not automatically mean verified
Promotion preflight fails closed on binding or semantic mismatches
entities.context: Runtime verification has backend, Termux, desktop, and mobile lanes and promotion is release- and source-bound.
entities.description: Tracked runtime documentation consumes sanitized promoted baselines, not arbitrary transient captures.
entities.name: Runtime evidence is explicitly promoted
runtime_implications: Documentation generation does not mutate runtime state
security_implications: Transient raw capture stays outside tracked outputs
trade_offs: Promotion is an explicit operator step
Tracked documentation stays deterministic, sanitized, and reviewable

consequences: Frontend never talks directly to NATS
entities.context: The canonical architecture requires UI to Caddy to FastAPI before NATS, workers, agents, supervisors, and evidence.
entities.description: Browser-facing control and command admission remain behind FastAPI rather than exposing execution backplanes to the PWA.
entities.name: FastAPI owns the browser-facing control API
runtime_implications: FastAPI availability is part of write readiness
security_implications: Backend secrets remain outside the browser
trade_offs: Centralizes validation, authorization, write safety, and audit evidence

alternatives: One global frontend store for backend truth
entities.context: The frontend must remain responsive without becoming an execution engine or durable backend authority.
entities.description: TanStack Query owns live server-state reads, Dexie stores safe read-only snapshots, Zustand owns harmless UI coordination, and XState owns guided workflow state.

runtime_implications: Saved state never proves current operational health
security_implications: Safe snapshots exclude secrets and write responses
